notes: First rate sweep with runtime shared BBR grants and ACK application; selective payload repair and complete loss-before-PTO ordering remain unfinished.

The same daemons, TAPs and sockets persist across 16G, 21G, unlimited and 16G return. No owned builds or other tests overlap the workload. Static musl release binaries use the documented release profile.
Directions are L->R and R->L. Endpoint arrays are L/R. Receiver samples measure application UDP payload goodput without the drain; full-run missing fractions include the drain. 100% CPU is one CPU.
Prior expiry observations used 60 seconds and predate other sender changes; they are historical context, not a matched causal before/after comparison.

All points have zero received invalid, duplicate, too-old and wrong-run records, admission pressure, and outer fragmentation. Outer socket overflow is zero. TAP drops and sender frame expiry dominate observed drop counters; units differ and cannot be added to reconstruct exact inner loss.

Goodput near 0.7 Gbit/s with ~1.6-1.7 CPUs per daemon is a severe integration regression, not the CPU maximum. Grant/feedback scheduling and controller behavior need profiling. Missing payload repair is not sufficient attribution.
worker_counter_deltas includes gauge differences only for raw completeness; use worker_gauges_after for final gauges. These after-drain gauges do not describe steady-load pacing/window state.
No acceptance gate passes; one short sweep is not the required repeated performance validation.
